subject: Duplicate monthly charge
description: Fictional support case: a customer reports two monthly subscription charges.

notes.author: support-reporter
notes.body: Agent report: customer says the duplicate charge affects their budget. No refund approval is recorded.

messages.body: I am worried. I see two monthly charges, and I need the extra one returned. Email demo-customer@example.invalid if we disconnect.
messages.speaker: support-customer

messages.body: I can submit the duplicate-charge review. I cannot confirm a refund today.
messages.speaker: support-agent

messages.body: Correction: the second charge is from September, not October. Please check September.
messages.speaker: support-customer

messages.body: There is another issue: I no longer receive invoices. Please restore invoice emails as well.
messages.speaker: support-customer

messages.body: I have submitted the review, but the refund decision is still pending. The invoice email change is not completed.
messages.speaker: support-agent

messages.body: I feel less worried now that the review is submitted, but I still need the money and the invoice emails.
messages.speaker: support-customer

guidance.text: Fictional demonstration guidance: confirm the disputed month before submitting a review. This is not client-approved policy.

messages.body: Two annual plan charges posted today. I need the extra charge returned.
messages.speaker: variant-customer

messages.body: The duplicate annual-plan charge was reversed today; your bank posting date is unknown.
messages.speaker: variant-agent

messages.body: I can see one reversal in my account now. I still do not know when the bank will finish posting it.
messages.speaker: variant-customer

subject: Login report
description: Fictional case report: a customer cannot sign in after replacing a device.

notes.author: note-reporter
notes.body: Agent report: customer wants access restored and says the old device is unavailable. No direct customer words were recorded. An access check is proposed; completion is unknown.

timing.availability: relative offsets only; wall-clock timestamps were not supplied

segments.transcript: I want a twelve-seat annual plan, but our budget is at most 900 units. I am anxious about committing before our security review.
I can send a proposal for review. I cannot promise a discount.
Correction, we need ten seats, not twelve. The budget stays at 900 units.
Before I decide, I also need to know whether data can stay in our chosen region. That is a separate security concern.
The region question is unanswered. I have only offered to send a proposal; no agreement is signed.
I feel calmer after separating the questions, but I will not sign until security confirms the region.

messages.body: I can offer six crates for 120 units if delivery is before Friday.
messages.speaker: peer-a

messages.body: I can supply four crates by Friday, or six next week.
messages.speaker: peer-b

messages.body: I need four this week then. Also, two must be reusable crates; disposable ones will not work.
messages.speaker: peer-a

messages.body: I need to check reusable stock. That is not confirmed yet.
messages.speaker: peer-b

messages.body: Then the order is pending. I am not accepting until reusable stock is confirmed.
messages.speaker: peer-a
